title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is navigating a complex landscape as military interests clash with bureaucratic hurdles, while private firms continue to chase scalability and innovation. Meanwhile, funding for space resilience is on the rise, hinting at a growing recognition of the strategic importance of space.

themes.title: Military and Bureaucratic Tensions
themes.body: The military space boom is facing friction in the Beltway, highlighting the challenges of aligning strategic goals with legislative processes. As defense budgets swell, the tug-of-war between innovation and regulation becomes increasingly evident.

themes.title: Funding and Scalability in Space
themes.body: With the FY27 budget markup adding $1.4B to space resilience, investors are keenly watching how companies like Terran Orbital navigate scalability. The influx of capital could either fuel rapid growth or exacerbate existing inefficiencies.

themes.title: New Partnerships and Initiatives
themes.body: Anduril and L3Harris are teaming up for a tactical SDA constellation bid, reflecting a trend of collaboration in an increasingly competitive landscape. These partnerships may prove crucial as companies seek to leverage shared expertise and resources.

themes.title: Emerging Technologies and Trends
themes.body: The recent surge in AI-focused defense startups signals a shift in technological priorities within the sector. As firms like Anthropic consider utilizing SpaceX's orbital data center, the intersection of AI and space capabilities is set to redefine operational paradigms.
